items.evidence: After `page.reload()` the spec checks `statusInfo` is "Unfulfilled" and the fulfil button is visible (diff lines 73-76). Those values come back from the server, so they would fail if the cancel mutation never ran.
"Unfulfilled" status after confirming is checked at diff line 65, the fulfil action reappearing at lines 66-67, and the status after reload at lines 73-75. All three acceptance criteria are covered.

No existing helper is duplicated. It reuses `OrderPage.goto`, `statusInfo`, `fulfillButton`, `timelineView` and `dialog`, plus `findOrderId` and `ORDERS_SCENARIO`. `OrderPage` has no cancel-fulfillment locators, so the new ones copy nothing.
No `waitForTimeout`, sleeps or polling loops. The waits are on the dialog hiding and on web-first assertions.
`test` and `expect` come from `../../fixtures/test.ts` (diff line 11). The test is not tagged `parallel()` and writes nothing to the cache or dumps.

Elements are found by test ids and by role and name. The dialog's `submit` is scoped to `orderPage.dialog` (line 58), and the warehouse select is scoped to the dialog (lines 29-31). There are no CSS, XPath or positional selectors.
The spec starts from the scenario's existing fulfilled order via `findOrderId(config, "fulfilled")` (line 35). It sets up no state through the API or the UI.
No hard-coded ids; the order is looked up by its scenario key. The warehouse name "Europe" is fixed seed data that populatedb does not randomise, and the ticket allows any warehouse.
No UI login. It uses the fixture's default `admin` actor, which suits a story with no permission given, and no credentials are typed in.
`typecheck.txt` reports "exit 0: no errors", and the file is under `e2e/tests/orders/`.

e2e/tests/orders/order-cancel-fulfillment.spec.ts:27-31 and 40-59: the fulfillment-menu, cancel-menu-item and warehouse-select locators, and the whole multi-step cancel flow, are written inline in the spec instead of as locators and a `cancelFulfillment` method on `OrderPage`.
No page-object members were added or changed.
`// Arrange`, `// Act` and `// Assert` comments appear at diff lines 25, 39 and 62.
It is one test for one story, with `test.step` for the cancel, the immediate check and the reload check.
The title "Cancelling a fulfillment returns the order to unfulfilled #e2e" describes the behaviour and carries the tag.
A doc comment at diff lines 15-18 says what the spec covers.
All assertions are web-first `await expect(locator)...` calls; nothing is read out of the page and then asserted.

The order comes from the scenario key and `ORDERS_SCENARIO` is imported. The remaining literals are UI status text and a warehouse name that has no scenario constant. No money or arithmetic is involved.
No cleanup hooks, and no random or timestamped names.
No explicit timeouts, retries, `networkidle` or `waitForLoadState`.
All relative imports keep `.ts`, and nothing is imported from `@playwright/test`.
No `any`, casts or untyped `gql` calls.

e2e/tests/orders/order-cancel-fulfillment.spec.ts:1-2 and 34-72: generator boilerplate (`// spec: specs/...`, `// seed: ...`) plus numbered step comments ("// 3. Open the fulfillment card's \"Show more\" menu", "// 8. Reload the page and check the state again") that restate the next line instead of explaining why.

structured_output.summary: The change is sound: it checks the order is still "Unfulfilled" after a reload, so a cancel that never reached the server would fail the test. It covers all three acceptance criteria, uses the fixture and the scenario's fulfilled order, and type-checks cleanly. Every blocker is met. Two minors fail: M1, because the cancel-fulfillment locators and the multi-step flow sit in the spec instead of on `OrderPage`, and M13, because of the generator boilerplate and numbered comments that restate each line.
